$comment: Thresholds, rates and ceilings. Kept OUT of the code so a tuning change is a config diff rather than a deploy of new logic, and out of the environment so it can be reviewed. Every credential it needs is referenced from process.env by name and never written here.

ingestion.$comment: Tens of thousands of mints are created a day and most never trade twice. These thresholds decide who gets the expensive pipeline.

activation.$note: Below both of these a token is a cheap SEEDED identity row: no security read, no holder sync, no scoring.

ingestion.$batchNote: DexScreener takes up to 30 comma-separated mints per request. Anything larger is silently truncated by them, which looks like missing tokens.

sellCheck.$comment: Two sources, in order. Observed sells beat a simulated route because they already happened.

calls.$comment: A call is rare BY CONSTRUCTION. Every gate below has to pass.
calls.$mcapNote: A gem finder that calls a token at a billion dollars has not made a claim anybody can act on — the move already happened. The ceiling is what keeps a call about something early; there is deliberately no MAXIMUM AGE, because a three-week-old token that finally clears the grade is exactly the call worth making.
calls.$timingNote: Of the first 79 calls, 41 never traded above their entry price. Every quality reading peaks when the price does, so a gate made only of quality thresholds fires at the top of the move by construction. These three are the veto on the MOMENT rather than on the token.
calls.$backtest: 18,362 hypothetical entries replayed over 83 tokens that clear the quality gates (scripts/backtest.ts). Median return one hour after entry, by how far the price had already run in the hour before: calm 0-30% 0.998 and 0% of entries fell 20%; hot 80-150% 0.886 and 41% fell 20%; ran 150-400% 0.783 and 58% fell; vertical >400% 0.528 and 82% fell. The first draft of these ceilings was 120% and 20%, which the sweep showed would have refused essentially nothing. They are set where the damage measurably begins, not where they look prudent.
calls.$fiveMinuteNote: 25, not the 10 first set from a single run. Two independent backtest windows disagreed about the 10-25% band — one put its median at 0.902, the other at 0.997 — on samples of 149 and 91 entries. They AGREED about 25-60%: 0.893 and 0.839, with 45% and 48% of entries down a fifth an hour later. The ceiling goes where both runs agree, not where one of them looked worse.
calls.$volumeNote: Lowered from 4,000 because the backtest showed that floor refusing a third of all entries with NO improvement in their outcome. It is kept at all for a reason the backtest cannot see: this is about being able to EXIT a position, not about predicting a return. The sell check tests that properly at size; this is the cheap indexable version of the same worry.

autotrade.$tickNote: Exits run at twice the rate of entries. A missed entry costs an opportunity; a missed exit costs the position.

gate.$note: Dollar value of ROCK an account must hold to arm the engine. ROCK_MINT overrides the mint; this is the line.
